questions.question: The historic Salt March was started by Mahatma Gandhi and his followers from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sabarmati Ashram**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The historic Salt March, also known as the Dandi March, was initiated by Mahatma Gandhi from the **Sabarmati Ashram** on March 12, 1930.
 
• This march was a significant act of civil disobedience against the British salt monopoly in colonial India.
 
• Gandhi and his followers marched approximately 240 miles to the coastal village of Dandi, where they made salt from seawater, defying British laws.
 
• The march attracted worldwide attention and was a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement, showcasing the power of nonviolent protest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sabarmati Ashram**, also known as Gandhi Ashram, was one of the residences of Mahatma Gandhi who lived there for about 12 years along with his wife, Kasturba Gandhi.
 
• The ashram served as one of the main centers of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• It is located in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, on the banks of the River Sabarmati.
 
• The ashram is now a national monument and a museum, preserving the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: Who is considered as the ‘linchpin of the Government’?

options.text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

__
 
• The **Prime Minister** is considered the 'linchpin of the Government'.
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and is responsible for running the government and implementing laws.
 
• The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the government and is the chief advisor to the President.
 
• The Prime Minister plays a crucial role in formulating and executing government policies and decisions.
 
• As the leader of the majority party in the Parliament, the Prime Minister ensures the stability and functionality of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Prime Minister** is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and presides over cabinet meetings.
 
• The Prime Minister represents the country in various international platforms and negotiations.
 
• In case of a coalition government, the Prime Minister is usually the leader of the largest party in the coalition.
 
• The Prime Minister plays a key role in the appointment of various constitutional and statutory bodies.
 
• The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) is an important part of the government machinery, assisting the Prime Minister in various functions.
 
• The Prime Minister can also recommend the dissolution of the Lok Sabha to the President.

questions.question: Post 1857 revolt, the Peel commission was set up to give on recommendations on ________ reorganisation of British India.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Post 1857 revolt, the Peel commission was set up to give recommendations on the **military** reorganization of British India.
 
• The commission was established to address the weaknesses and failures of the British military forces that were exposed during the revolt.
 
• It focused on restructuring the army, improving the recruitment process, and ensuring better coordination and efficiency within the military ranks.
 
• The recommendations aimed to prevent any future uprisings and to maintain British dominance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 1857 revolt, also known as the Indian Mutiny or the First War of Independence, was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising against the British East India Company's rule.
 
• The revolt led to significant changes in British policies and governance in India, including the transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown.
 
• The Peel Commission's recommendations were part of broader efforts to stabilize British control and prevent any similar revolts in the future.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 148**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 148** of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is an authority, established by the Constitution of India under Chapter V, who audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and the state governments, including those of bodies and authorities substantially financed by the government.
 
• The CAG is appointed by the President of India and can only be removed from office in a manner and on the grounds specified for the removal of a Supreme Court judge.
 
• The office of the CAG is crucial for maintaining transparency and accountability in the financial administration of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The role of the CAG has been expanded over time to include auditing of various public sector enterprises and autonomous bodies.

questions.question: The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the Government of India Act, ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the Government of India Act, **1935**.
 
• The Government of India Act 1935 was a comprehensive statute that laid the foundation for the federal structure and significant administrative reforms in British India.
 
• Provisions under this act included the establishment of a Federal Court, the division of powers between the centre and provinces, and emergency powers.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopted many features from this act, including the emergency provisions allowing the President to declare an emergency in case of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• These emergency provisions ensure that the central government can take swift and decisive action to maintain the sovereignty, security, and integrity of the country during times of crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Government of India Act 1935** was the last pre-independence constitution of India, and it served as the basis for the Constitution of India adopted in 1950.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy, which allowed Indian provinces to govern themselves to a certain extent, reducing the powers of the British Governor-General.
 
• The Act also provided for the establishment of a Federal Court and outlined a federal structure for India, which influenced the federal nature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Many principles and administrative structures established by the 1935 Act were retained and refined in the Indian Constitution, contributing to the stability and continuity of governance post-independence.
 
• Emergency provisions were necessary to tackle unforeseen situations that could threaten the nation, thereby providing a constitutional mechanism to handle crises effectively.

questions.question: What is the name of the cold phase of the ENSO climate pattern that describes the unusual cooling of the surface waters of the region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**La Nina**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **La Nina** is the cold phase of the ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) climate pattern.
 
• It describes the unusual cooling of the surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
 
• La Nina events typically bring about a variety of weather changes, including increased rainfall in some regions and drought in others.
 
• This phenomenon is the opposite of El Niño, which is the warm phase of the ENSO climate pattern.
 
• La Nina can influence global weather patterns and has significant impacts on agriculture, water supply, and hurricane activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ENSO cycle includes both El Niño and La Nina phases, as well as periods of neutral conditions.
 
• La Nina events are characterized by stronger-than-average trade winds, which push warm water towards the western Pacific, allowing cold water to upwell in the eastern Pacific.
 
• The cooling effect of La Nina can last for several months and typically occurs every 2 to 7 years.
 
• La Nina can also influence the Atlantic hurricane season, often leading to more active hurricane periods.
 
• Scientists monitor the ENSO cycle using various tools, including satellite observations and ocean buoys, to predict and understand its impacts.

questions.question: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harry Hammond Hess**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harry Hammond Hess** published 'The History of Ocean Basins' in 1962.
 
• His work outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, which later came to be known as 'sea floor spreading'.
 
• Hess's theory was crucial in providing a mechanism for Alfred Wegener's earlier hypothesis of continental drift.
 
• This theory helped to explain the formation of mid-ocean ridges and the symmetrical pattern of magnetic stripes on the ocean floor.
 
• Sea floor spreading is a key component of the broader theory of plate tectonics, which describes the movement of the Earth's lithosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alfred Wegener** proposed the theory of continental drift in 1912, suggesting that continents had once been joined together and had since drifted apart.
 
• **Louis Bauer** was an American geophysicist known for his work in geomagnetism but did not contribute to the theory of sea floor spreading.
 
• **George Edward Backus** was an American geophysicist known for his work in geophysical inverse theory and geomagnetism, but not related to sea floor spreading.
 
• The concept of plate tectonics has revolutionized our understanding of Earth's geological processes, including the formation of mountains, earthquakes, and volcanic activity.

questions.question: The cell wall of spirogyra contains:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cellulose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The cell wall of **spirogyra** contains **cellulose**.
 
• **Cellulose** is a polysaccharide consisting of a linear chain of several hundred to many thousands of β(1→4) linked D-glucose units.
 
• It is a primary structural component of green algae and plants, making up about 30% of their cell walls.
 
• Other substances like **lignin, suberin, and chitin** are found in different types of organisms or serve different functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is commonly found in freshwater habitats and is known for its role in photosynthesis.
 
• Cellulose in the cell wall provides structural support and protection, maintaining the shape and rigidity of the cells.

• The game is known for its physical endurance, agility, and strategic plays.

• The raider must chant "Kabaddi, Kabaddi" throughout the raid to prove they are not inhaling.
 
• The sport has gained international recognition and is played in many countries including Iran, South Korea, Japan, and Kenya.

The correct answer is __**the maximum number of individuals a species can produce**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biotic potential** refers to the **maximum reproductive capacity** of an organism under optimum environmental conditions.
 
• This concept is significant in population ecology as it helps to understand the growth potential of a species.
 
• The **biotic potential** is influenced by factors such as the organism's rate of reproduction and the duration of its reproductive life.
 
• It is an idealized concept assuming no limiting factors like food scarcity, predation, or disease, which in reality always exist to some extent.
 
• The actual population size is often lower than the biotic potential due to these environmental resistance factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding biotic potential is crucial for **conservation efforts** and managing species that are endangered or overpopulated.
 
• **Environmental resistance** includes all factors that limit the biotic potential of an organism, such as food availability, predation, disease, and habitat destruction.
 
• In practical terms, the biotic potential is rarely achieved in natural environments due to these limiting factors.
 
• Ecologists use the concept to model population growth and to predict how populations will respond to changes in environmental conditions.
 
• The study of biotic potential is part of **population ecology**, which examines the dynamics of species populations and how they interact with the environment.

questions.question: Which state of India does the musician Shyamamani Devi belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shyamamani Devi** is a renowned musician from the state of **Odisha**, India.
 
• She is celebrated for her contributions to **Odissi music**, which is a classical music genre from Odisha.
 
• Shyamamani Devi has been honored with several awards for her exceptional talent and dedication to the field of music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi music is one of the **classical music forms** of India and has a history that dates back several centuries.
 
• It is known for its **melodic and rhythmic intricacies** and is often performed during the Odissi dance.
 
• Shyamamani Devi's contributions have been instrumental in preserving and promoting this traditional art form.
